summary: Granular runtime-checkable capability protocols that storage backends implement a la carte: StorageReadProtocol, StorageWriteProtocol, StorageEnumerateProtocol, StorageDeleteProtocol, StorageMetadataProtocol, StorageCopyProtocol, StorageDirectoryProtocol and the optional RangedReadProtocol. The docstrings fix cross-backend semantics: typed StorageError subclasses instead of raw SDK errors, create_parents behaviour, path_exists returning False only for established absence, and the delimiter/recursion rules for list_objects. StorageFacade uses isinstance checks against these protocols for supports() and to raise UnsupportedOperationError.
key_classes: StorageWriteProtocol — write_from_bytes / write_from_stream with keyword-only create_parents=True (no-op on object/HTTP backends)
StorageMetadataProtocol — get_metadata -> StorageEntry, path_exists, get_size -> int | None
StorageCopyProtocol — copy(source, destination) within one backend
StorageDirectoryProtocol — list_dir -> list[StorageEntry], mkdir(path, *, parents=True), rmdir
RangedReadProtocol — open_ranged(path) -> RangedSource for random-access reads (HTTP, S3, SFTP)
extension_points: Custom backends implement any subset structurally; capability is detected with isinstance (runtime_checkable)
tests/storage/protocols/test_backend_conformance.py pins the expected protocol set per registered provider; a new backend or capability needs a row there
lifecycle_notes: Stdlib-only imports (plus _core dataclasses/ranged_io); importable on a base install
Current coverage: local implements all seven core protocols; S3 family all but Directory; SFTP Read/Write/Delete/Metadata/Directory/Enumerate; HTTP Read/Write/Metadata; RangedRead on HTTP, S3, SFTP
documentation_hooks: Capability matrix per backend (generated from conformance expectations)
Error contract: which typed StorageError each operation may raise and when (read vs close)
Writing a backend: protocol method signatures and semantic obligations
create_parents semantics across directory and object backends
examples: examples/capability_checks/example.py — storage.supports(Protocol) on local vs https and UnsupportedOperationError for list_dir on HTTP
risks: runtime_checkable isinstance only checks method presence, not signatures; a backend missing the keyword-only create_parents argument still satisfies StorageWriteProtocol at runtime (README warns custom backends must accept it)
